title: B2 and C2: T13 applies the C2 adjustment of SPEC 6.4 in site code instead of taking its display records from satakeRecord
claim: The restricted board name and the Bourbaki order that T13 displays are rebuilt in site code from satake(d), with a second copy of the C2 rule. The satakeRecord records that matchCatalogue returns are read only for their names, so the 6.4 naming rule now has two implementations, one outside the engine.
expected: SPEC 6.4: 'This adjustment is made by satake_record (engine: satakeRecord); the plain function satake would say B2.' SPEC Appendix H, Rules (also in CLAUDE.md): 'Satake records for display come from satakeRecord, which applies the C2 naming of SPEC 6.4.'
observed: model.ts:445 `if (r.restricted_type_display === 'C2' && restrictedBoardName === 'B2' && order !== null) {`, 446 `restrictedBoardName = 'C2';`, 447 `order = order.reverse();`, applied to satake(d)'s restricted_board and restricted_orbits_in_bourbaki_order. Every displayed value is right today: called with the reader's own pair, satakeRecord(name, {...record, black_nodes, tau}) gives the same restricted_board and orbits on every catalogue pair and every symmetry image of rank at most 6, so the fix is a call to the engine.
reproduction: From a clean checkout of f07eec6 plus the reproducer: npm ci --prefer-offline; npx vitest run site/tests/unit/redteam-RT-02-p6-c2-once.test.ts. The first test fails and lists model.ts:445, 446 and 447; the second test passes.
specRef: SPEC.md 6.4 'Names in rank 2' ('This adjustment is made by satake_record (engine: satakeRecord)'); Appendix H Rules; RT-02 attack 13. decisions/P6-A3.md records that the plan's instruction 5.6 asked for the site-side adjustment.
proposedFix: In assembleData, take restricted_board and restricted_orbits_in_bourbaki_order from satakeRecord(boardName, {...record, black_nodes: X, tau}) for the reader's own pair, and delete the site branch. The plan directed the current design, so this may need the orchestrator's decision.

refute.citation: SPEC.md 6.4 'Names in rank 2' (unlabelled): 'This adjustment is made by `satake_record` (engine: `satakeRecord`); the plain function `satake` would say `B2`.' SPEC.md Appendix H, Rules: 'Satake records for display come from satakeRecord, which applies the C2 naming of SPEC 6.4.' Both sentences support the finding's expected. decisions/P6-A3.md 'P6-A3: the C2 drawing rule' and DECISIONS.md 'MERGE: P6 stage 6.2, P6-A3 (T13 Satake Studio)' ruling (1) record which record decides the drawing. They do not record an exemption from 6.4 or Appendix H for applying the adjustment in site code.
refute.evidence: I read everything in the worktree, detached at f07eec6; git status --porcelain was empty before and after. (1) site/src/components/tools/t13/model.ts lines 443-448, in assembleData: `if (r.restricted_type_display === 'C2' && restrictedBoardName === 'B2' && order !== null) { restrictedBoardName = 'C2'; order = order.reverse(); }`. It is applied to satake(d)'s restricted_board and restricted_orbits_in_bourbaki_order. The records from matchCatalogue (satakeRecord output) are read only for real_form, cartan_label and restricted_type_display. This matches the finding's observed. (2) SPEC 6.4 'Names in rank 2' has no [D] and no 'may'. The only [D] on rank-2 names is in 2.8 (line 319: the 'B2=C2' display). D19 (section 10) covers picker names and the 'B2=C2' note, not where the Satake adjustment is made. (3) SPEC 4 T13 (phase 6): 'Restricted board: drawn in Bourbaki order (`restricted_orbits_in_bourbaki_order`)', and names come from `matchCatalogue`. SPEC 5.3 has the row `satakeRecord(name, entry)`: 'the complete record of section 6.4 ... and the C2 adjustment described there'. CONTRACTS 2.4 has `satakeRecord(name: string, entry: SatakeCatalogueEntry): SatakeRecord`. (4) Plan instruction P6-A3 5.6 directs the site-side adjustment ('when the record you draw by has restricted_type_display C2, name the restricted board C2 and reverse ...; Record the rule; it is an open question for the orchestrator'). Its own trap list (section 9) says 'The C2 adjustment is satakeRecord's, not satake's'. (5) decisions/P6-A3.md line 22 records the rule ('Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.6)'). It names as left open only 'which record decides the drawing when two match'. (6) P6-A3.json openQuestions: 'C2 drawing rule: draw by the record whose pair is the reader's, else the first record (D4 black 3, 4: so(2,6), B2).' MERGE ruling (1): 'the C2 drawing rule stands (the record whose pair is the reader's, else the first record; on D4 black 3, 4 so(2,6), drawn B2)'. The question and the ruling are both about which record decides. The finding does not contest that. (7) The 'Note for T13' in 'MERGE: P6-A1 reviewed' is about laying the board out by labels and says nothing on where the C2 adjustment lives. (8) The known-and-decided list in P6-LENS-INSTRUCTIONS.md does not name the C2 rule. reports/gate-G6.md (from the integration branch) names f07eec6 as the gate commit and has no open item on it. There is no earlier P6 red-team merge report. I read the reproducer as text: test 1 greps model.ts for the C2 branch; test 2 compares assembleData with satakeRecord on the reader's pair.
refute.reason: not refuted: R1 failed: 6.4 and Appendix H are unqualified, and T13's spec text names the record field. R2 failed: the finding quotes both sentences correctly, and assembleData does build the displayed restricted_board and Bourbaki orbits itself. R3 failed: T13 and satakeRecord are phase 6 and the gate is G6. R4 failed: the finding concedes every value is right, so there is no value for the oracle to settle. R5 failed: the sentence is not [D], the default is the plan's (not a section 10 default and not the owner's answer), and the logged decision and MERGE ruling (1) settle only which record decides the drawing, not the second implementation of the adjustment in site code; a plan-directed departure from an unlabelled rule is not covered (RT-VERIFY 5.4). R6 failed: no gate item or earlier-round record. Minor fits: values are right, the duplication is structural.

title: Position for label: T13 converts the labels of the drawn restricted board to array indices with `l - 1`, `k - 1` and `k + 1` outside toLabels/toPositions
claim: T13 turns a node label of the drawn restricted board (boardFromName of the restricted board's name) into an index of the Bourbaki-ordered arrays (drawing.orbits, pairs, orbitIndex, coordinates) by subtracting one, and writes labels back by adding one, in 12 places. RestrictedBoardView.svelte converts the same labels with toLabels and toPositions.
expected: SPEC 5.1 E-7: 'Two functions, toLabels and toPositions, convert node lists and words; nothing else converts.'
observed: Twelve lines, for example `drawn.labels.map((l) => String(coords[l - 1]!))`, `drawing.orbitIndex[k - 1]` and `${k + 1}: (${a}, ${b})`. Every value is right, because every drawn restricted board is a named finite board whose labels are 1..m in position order. Lens section 6 rates such a conversion minor.
reproduction: From a clean checkout of f07eec6 plus the reproducer: npm ci --prefer-offline; npx vitest run site/tests/unit/redteam-RT-02-p6-label-arith.test.ts. One test fails and lists the 12 lines.
specRef: SPEC.md 5.1 E-7 ('nothing else converts'); RT-02 attack 1 and section 6.
proposedFix: Index the Bourbaki-ordered arrays by toPositions(drawn, [l])[0], and write the drawn node's label with toLabels(drawn, [k])[0].

Two functions, toLabels and toPositions, convert node lists and words; nothing else converts.' The sentence supports the finding's expected. refute.evidence: I confirmed every cited line at f07eec6. model.ts:521 `${k + 1}: (${a}, ${b})`; 527 `drawing.orbits[k - 1]`; 528 `drawing.pairs[k - 1]`; 534 `data.drawing!.orbits[k - 1]`; 732 `drawing.orbitIndex[k - 1]`; 859 `at node ${k + 1}`; 875 `at node ${k + 1}`. Here `drawn` is boardFromName of the restricted name, and the arrays are in its Bourbaki or position order, so each line converts a drawn-board label to a position (or back) by hand. RestrictedBoardView.svelte imports and uses toLabels and toPositions (lines 9, 44, 53, 55), as the finding says. E-7's table defines restricted-board labels as 1..m in Bourbaki order. It gives no exception to 'nothing else converts'. The 'Note for T13' in 'MERGE: P6-A1 reviewed' says 'lay the restricted board out by its labels, not by its name', which does not permit by-hand arithmetic. The project has already treated index arithmetic over a list in label or Bourbaki order as an E-7 conversion (P3-RT-02-02 on T9, confirmed and fixed; the T11 repair). RT-02 lens file section 6: 'A conversion written as board.labels[k] that gives the right value: report as minor only, citing E-7's nothing else converts'. The known-and-decided list says nothing on this. gate-G6 has no item on it, and there is no earlier P6 round record.
refute.reason: not refuted: R1 failed: E-7's 'nothing else converts' has no qualifier and no [D]. R2 failed: the lines turn drawn-board labels into indices of position-ordered arrays and back, which the project's own precedents (P3-RT-02-02, the T11 repair) treat as E-7 conversions. R3 failed: T13 is phase 6 and the gate is G6. R4 failed: no value disagreement (every value is right, as the finding says). R5 failed: decisions/P6-A3.md and plan 5.9 record the label-k-to-k-th-orbit mapping, not an exemption from toLabels/toPositions, and the same plan calls them the only converters. R6 failed: no record. Minor matches the lens rubric for a by-hand conversion that gives the right value.

title: T13's node buttons carry data-board values 'decoration' and 'restricted' and data-value 'black' and 'white', outside the hooks of 4.0

The restricted board, where the shadows play a mutation game (2.15), uses data-board="restricted" instead of populations. The text of the [D] rule is departed from, though the departure is logged.

refute.citation: SPEC.md 4.0 [D] Test hooks: 'Every node button carries data-node (its label), data-board (populations or numbers, which matters in the linked view), data-value (the value shown, as decimal text, or as p/q for a fraction) and data-can-act (true or false).' SPEC 2.15: 'So the shadows carry a mutation game of their own, on the restricted board ...'. The passage supports the finding for the restricted board.
refute.evidence: 4.0 is [D] at its heading, and its Test hooks sentence names exactly two data-board values. DECISIONS.md '2026-10-25 P6-A3: the data-out names and the extra hooks (deviation to confirm)' records data-board="decoration" with data-value the colour, and data-board="restricted' with the stated reason '4.0 names only populations and numbers; a third value keeps the Challenge component's reading of the game board's populations clean'. The builder itself calls this a deviation. Neither 'MERGE: P6 stage 6.2, P6-A3' (rulings 1 to 3: C2 drawing, whereToRun, data-moves) nor 'MERGE: P6-A3 reviewed; rulings' nor 'MERGE: P6-A3 and P6-A4 repaired after review' rules on it. The review's 'confirmed ... the hooks' refers, in P6-A3-review.json, to 'the four 4.0 hooks are on every node button', that is, presence, not values. A partial refutation exists for the paint buttons: the decoration shows neither populations nor numbers, and the P6-A3 plan (line 188) itself makes them 'a hook outside 4.0's list'. That does not reach the restricted board, whose values are shadow coordinates. By 2.15 these carry a mutation game, so 4.0's 'populations' applies, and the third value departs from the [D] text for convenience. RT-VERIFY 5.4: 'R5 holds for a choice within the [D] text, never for a departure from it.' Lines read at f07eec6: DecorationDiagram.svelte:138 and RestrictedBoardView.svelte:92 carry the values the finding names.
refute.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because 4.0 lists only populations and numbers with no 'may', and 2.15 makes the restricted board's values populations of a mutation game; R2 failed, because the finding quotes 4.0 exactly, and the reading that 4.0 cannot apply holds only for the paint buttons, which leaves the restricted-board part standing; R3 failed, because T13 is phase 6; R4 does not apply; R5 failed, because P6-A3 logged a departure 'to confirm' that MERGE never ruled on, and a departure from [D] text is not R5; R6 failed, because nothing is on record. Severity: the rubric of RED-TEAM-COMMON 4 lists 'a hook' wrong under major.

title: A link to /tools/satake/ fetches 92297 B of JavaScript before the first interaction: T13 loads its typeset-name chunk while the island hydrates (166 of the 167 Atlas links)
location: site/src/components/tools/T13SatakeStudio.svelte:325-330 (the hydration $effect calls readLink), :311-321 (readLink calls setConfig when the link names another pair) and :303-308 (setConfig calls loadNames); site/src/components/tools/t13/names.ts:15-21 (loadNames imports t13/satakeNames.ts, chunk _astro/satakeNames.*.js)
claim: When the URL names a pair other than the configured one, T13's hydration effect goes through setConfig, which calls loadNames. The typeset-name chunk (5230 B gzip) is then fetched with no input, so /tools/satake/ opened from a link fetches 92297 B before the reader's first interaction, over the 90 kB of a tool alone. /embed/satake/ behaves the same.
expected: SPEC 7.6: a tool alone on /tools/<id> stays within 90 kB, counted as 'all JavaScript the route fetches before the reader's first interaction'. SPEC 6.6: on a tool's own route the link keys are bare, so a link opens the same route. decisions/P6-A3.md ('the names of real forms, typeset at build time and loaded lazily'): the names load 'in the browser only after the reader's first change of decoration or of panel ..., because the section weighs about 5 kB gzipped and the route measured 85.0 of its 90 kB without it'.
observed: Root preview build of f07eec6: the default /tools/satake/ is 87067 B (18 scripts); 166 of the 167 'Open this real form in the Satake Studio' links on the 32 Atlas pages each measure 92297 B, with the only extra script satakeNames.MjFZAB5c.js at 5230 B. The exception is the link equal to the default pair, A3 x=2 t=3.2.1, at 87067 B. The E7 and E8 links also fetch the worker script (24098 B, not counted). The committed spec fails on its 3 link cases with 'Expected <= 90000, Received 92297' ('scripts beyond the default state: satakeNames.MjFZAB5c.js 5230'); its control (the default route) passes. npm run size cannot see this, because it opens bare routes only.
reproduction: From a clean checkout of f07eec6 plus this branch: npm ci --prefer-offline; npm run build; PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<pw> npx playwright test -c redteam/redteam-RT-07-p6-playwright.config.ts redteam-RT-07-p6-link-size.spec.ts. Result: 3 failed (links A3 x=1.3, D8 x=1.3.5.7, E6 x=2.3.4.5), 1 passed (control). The config hard-codes this worktree's path in WT; edit WT for another checkout. The full sweep: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<pw> node redteam/redteam-RT-07-p6-link-sweep.mjs site/dist / 5572 <scratch>/links.json /satake/ 3 prints '167 links measured; 166 over the limit of their route'.
specRef: SPEC.md 7.6 (table row 'each tool alone, on /tools/<id> | 90 kB'; 'all JavaScript the route fetches before the reader's first interaction'); SPEC.md 6.6 ('On a tool's own route (/tools/..., /embed/...) the keys are bare'); decisions/P6-A3.md 2026-10-25 'the names of real forms, typeset at build time and loaded lazily'
proposedFix: Fetch the names only from the reader's own actions (paint, tau, pick, example, catalogue entry, openPanel). readLink should load the link's pair without loadNames, keeping the plain-markup names that names.ts already writes until the first change. Adopting the committed spec keeps a link state under 90 kB, which npm run size does not check.
